entries.text: This is the company HQ. Use the telephone on the central dispatch bench ({key:Interact}) to pick today's job. The field guide is beside it.
Job taken. Grab gear and upgrades at the maintenance bench, then get in the van ({key:Interact}) when the crew is ready.
Scan ({key:Scan}) to reveal prices and haul. Carry loot to the loading-bay truck and pull the yellow lever to leave. Its board shows your quota.
{key:Interact} picks things up. Heavier loot slows you down; fragile loot loses value when it hits something.
Small things go straight into your pockets. Hold {key:Inventory} to see them ({key:Inventory} + {key:Drop} drops the last).
Too heavy for one person: grab a handle together with your crew to lift it, or drag it alone (slow, and it still weighs on the floor).
Hold {key:Rotate} + mouse to turn it. Tap {key:Drop} to drop, hold {key:Drop} to set it down gently; hold {key:Use} to throw. Careful with glass.
The floor is cracking under the weight! Spread out, drop something heavy or get off it before it gives way.
The power is out. {key:Flashlight} turns your flashlight on.
Something is clicking in the dark. The Blind One hunts by sound: crouch ({key:Crouch}), don't run, don't drop things.
Something is watching you. The Stalker only moves when nobody looks at it: keep an eye on it, and don't wander off alone.
Something wants your loot. The Collector steals what's left lying around and runs; chase it and it drops it.
You died. Watch your crew as a ghost; the living can't hear you. A nearby crewmate with a medkit can revive you.
Something big is patrolling. If it sees you it charges: break line of sight, slide a door shut behind you, hide in a locker, or sprint. It's heavy, and weak floors don't hold it.
The truck is leaving! Get in the bay before the honking stops, or you're left behind.
A locked store. What's behind a shutter is worth more. Bolt cutters open it quietly; a crowbar opens it loudly (both from the HQ shop).
The answering machine is blinking: the boss left you a message.
Doors slide ({key:Interact}). A shut door blocks sight, and most things can't open one. The Hunter breaks down a door it saw you go through: that takes it a few blows, and everyone hears them.
You can hide in a locker ({key:Interact}, hands empty). Nothing that hunts by sight finds you in there, unless it watched you climb in. Sound still carries.
A breaker panel ({key:Interact}). Throwing it lights this part of the building for two minutes, but the bang and the hum carry, and things come to see.
The freight lift ({key:Interact}) is slow and loud, and it needs power. Mind the weight on the deck: overloaded, it gives way halfway.
A vent. Crouch and press {key:Interact} to crawl through to wherever it comes out. Nothing follows you in there, but the duct rattles, and only what fits in your pockets comes with you.
An alarm box. A blinking lamp means this store is wired: walk in and the bell rings for half a minute, and everything that hears it comes. Bolt cutters ({key:Interact} at the box) cut it.
A safe. Set the drill on it ({key:Interact}) and it is through in a minute and a half, but it is the loudest thing in the building, and it jams: someone has to stay and free it.
The security desk ({key:Interact}). Whoever sits here sees the cameras and can talk the crew round the building, but they can't see what is behind them.
The loot catalogue ({key:Interact}). Every kind of salvage the company has sold gets a line; every jackpot gets a place on the trophy shelf.
The agency radio ({key:Interact}). A dead crewmate can come back as a new hire, standing in the truck. The fee comes out of the payout.
The difficulty switch. Relaxed, Standard or Brutal: it moves the quota, how hard monsters hit, how often they come and how fast the building falls apart. Only the host turns it.
